statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 4, low, because CME equity index futures have been halted since Friday at 21:00Z and twenty of the twenty-four hours published here contain no tradable interval at all; only the four slots from the scheduled 22:00Z Sunday reopen onward are tradable, and they carry conditional Tail readings of 12, 13, 12 and 11 that stay far below the block threshold. Stress is 36, moderate: a 50% US tariff on Canadian goods is live after the collapse of trade talks, Canada has dated a dollar-for-dollar match to 8 September, the 20 August H.15 column shows 4.19% at two years, 4.69% at ten and 5.23% at thirty with the long end at its highest since 2007, and Brent at $94.39 with WTI at $87.06 completes a second consecutive weekly energy gain. Confidence is 87, high: Friday's closing levels were cross-checked against independent public sources after one quote page returned an inconsistent level alongside its own delayed-data warning, and the shared cross-asset context read this hour was fresh and complete.
recommendation: The last observed session remains consistent with functioning mean reversion rather than a one-way path: cash NDX opened at 29,359.60, traded down to 29,142.44, recovered to 29,405.12 and closed at 29,308.86, up 0.33% on the day and below its own open, ending a five-day losing streak, while the VIX settled at 14.89 near the low of a 14.77-15.95 range. Both session extremes were retraced and neither produced repeated extension after a failed pullback, so no Tail amplifier carries over from observed structure. Friday internals were split rather than aligned, with software firm, semiconductors net lower and megacaps five to three higher on roughly 1.8 points of dispersion. Because the venue is shut for twenty of the twenty-four hours published here, the first Tail-relevant evidence can only come from prints after the 22:00Z Sunday reopen: whether an opening gap is retraced, whether pullbacks appear, and whether yields, energy and volatility align or conflict once they can trade against equities again. Until then the assessment is retrospective by construction, and the published danger window is deliberately narrow rather than a broad weekend shutdown.
headline: Closed-venue assessment with four reopen hours inside the horizon: Tail holds the floor of 4 through twenty shut hours, then carries conditional readings of 12, 13, 12 and 11 from the 22:00Z Sunday reopen, while live US tariffs on Canadian goods, a post-2007 long end and a second week of energy gains stay unpriced.
body: CME Globex equity index futures stopped trading for the week on Friday at 21:00Z and are scheduled to reopen on Sunday at 22:00Z. The twenty-four slots published here run from 2026-08-23T02:00:00Z to 2026-08-24T01:00:00Z, so the reopen slot and the first three hours after it all sit inside the horizon. Cash NDX settled at 29,308.86 on Friday, up 0.33%, after opening at 29,359.60 and printing a 29,142.44 low and a 29,405.12 high; both extremes were retraced inside the session, the close finished below the open, and the day ended a five-day losing streak. That close was cross-checked against independent public sources this hour after one quote page returned an inconsistent level with its own delayed-data warning. On policy, the 50% US tariff on Canadian goods is in force after trade talks collapsed, and Prime Minister Carney has said Canada will match it dollar for dollar from 8 September, targeting sectors including steel, dairy, agricultural equipment and pulp and paper. On rates, the 10-year settled near 4.737% on Friday for its largest weekly gain since 31 July, and the 20 August H.15 column shows the thirty-year at 5.23%, the highest since 2007. Energy completed a second consecutive weekly gain of more than 5%, with Brent at $94.39 and WTI at $87.06, while Friday commentary noted signs that Iran may be seeking an end to its conflict with the US; no fresh escalation has been verified over the weekend. The shared cross-asset context read this hour was fresh, complete and internally consistent with Friday's tape: index futures modestly higher, the volatility future lower, Treasury futures lower across the curve and gold up 2.39%, with megacaps five to three higher and semiconductors net lower. None of that is live price-path evidence, and none of it establishes the persistent directional efficiency that Tail measures. Stress at 36 reflects a fixed but substantial stack of unpriced inputs that must be expressed in a single opening auction; Tail at 4 reflects the simple fact that a shut venue cannot produce a pathological price path. Conditional Tail rises only after the reopen, peaking at 13 in the first full hour, which is why the danger window covers 22:00Z Sunday through 02:00Z Monday and nothing wider.

lookbackSummary: Claude coverage over the past 24 hours is nearly complete: 21 hourly assessments are available, while the 05:00Z, 06:00Z and 21:00Z clock-hours have no published assessment and are marked unavailable. Across every available hour Tail held 4 and the mapped policy state stayed EA_ON, so no hour approached the block threshold and the dominant mode remained normal throughout. Stress traced a shallow arc: 36 at the start of the window, a rebuild to 42 through the middle of Saturday as the tariff deadline passed and the Canadian response was dated, then a steady easing to 37 by the final hour. Confidence stayed in an 85-88 band, reflecting verified closing levels and macro data set against the absence of any live price path. Nothing in the window contains observed one-way structure, because no venue was open to produce it.
outlookSummary: The current hour carries Tail at 4 because CME equity index futures are confirmed halted and no Nasdaq-100 price path can develop inside this slot. The following nineteen slots describe the same closed market, so Tail holds 4 and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout them. The last four slots are tradable: the 22:00Z scheduled reopen carries a conditional Tail of 12, the first full hour after it a conditional 13, the hour coinciding with the Monday Asian cash open a conditional 12, and the final slot a conditional 11, all still green and all resting on gap and thin-liquidity scenarios rather than on observed structure. They are the only reason a narrow danger window is published. Stress eases from 36 to a 34 trough through the Sunday overnight hours, rebuilds steadily to 46 in the final closed hour, peaks at 52 in the reopen slot as the weekend information set converges on a single opening auction, then eases to 45 as Asian liquidity arrives. Confidence declines from 87 to 72 across the horizon, which reflects distance from the assessment cutoff rather than any defect in the verified inputs.
